messages.subject: Negative AICc and error in detection estimates
parts:
Hi, 
I'm doing density estimations for a critically endangered frog. I have two short questions:
- Some analysis come out right but sometimes the AICc is negative, is this okey?
- Also, I run the density estimations and they are okey, but sometimes I get an error in the detection estimations

Error in .local(obj, coefficients, ...) : 
  type %in% names(obj) is not TRUE               

does this mean that I cannot trust the density estimations, that they are not correct?

Thank you

Rocío

On Tuesday, April 14, 2020 at 7:07:47 PM UTC-4, Rocío Seisdedos wrote:
Hi, 
I'm doing density estimations for a critically endangered frog. I have two short questions:
- Some analysis come out right but sometimes the AICc is negative, is this okey?

Yes - negative AIC values are legitimate and interpreted in the same way as positive AIC values. The negative AIC arises due to the portion of the multinomial coefficient that is computed. Frequently, for computational efficiency, terms are dropped from the likelihood expression that are not functions of the parameters of interest (usually ugly factyorial terms). This occasionally (often, for some data types)  which results in a negative AIC. .Regardless, the model with the ‘most negative’ AIC, i.e., the one furthest from zero, is the most parsimonious among the models in the candidate model set.
